items.title: Parent Beneficiary Birth Certificate
items.sub: The parent's official civil birth record

sections.c: Provide the birth certificate issued by the competent civil authority. For Pakistan, this may be issued through a Union Council, Cantonment Board, Municipal Corporation, CDA where applicable, or another authority recognized in the Department of State reciprocity schedule.

If the standard birth registration certificate is unavailable, follow the Pakistan reciprocity instructions regarding accepted alternate or secondary records. Do not substitute an informal family document without explaining why the primary record is unavailable.
The parent's name, date of birth, place of birth, and parents' names should be consistent with the passport, DS-260, and the petitioner's relationship evidence.

items.title: Petitioner's Birth Certificate
items.sub: Core IR-5 relationship record identifying the parent beneficiary

sections.c: For an IR-5 parent case, the petitioner's birth certificate is the central record showing the qualifying parent-child relationship. NVC instructions specifically identify the petitioner's original or certified birth certificate for IR-5 cases.
Confirm that the parent beneficiary is correctly named and that names, dates, and spellings are consistent with the approved I-130 petition and the parent's current identity documents.
Keep the original or a certified copy ready for the consular interview, even if a scan is uploaded to CEAC.

items.title: Police Certificate
items.sub: Pakistan Character Certificate and any other required police certificates for the parent

sections.c: The parent beneficiary generally needs police certificates under the Department of State's age and residence rules, including certificates from Pakistan and other countries where required.

For Pakistan, the relevant record is commonly called a Police Character Certificate or Character Certificate. Obtain it from the competent police authority according to the current Pakistan reciprocity instructions.

Police-certificate validity rules can affect interview readiness. If the certificate becomes too old or the applicant continues residing in the issuing country, an updated certificate may be required.

items.title: Parent Beneficiary Marriage Certificate
items.sub: Official civil proof of the parent's current or relevant marriage

sections.c: Prepare the parent's marriage record when CEAC requests it based on the parent's marital history, or when the marriage is relevant to the approved parent-child relationship.
For a Muslim marriage registered in Pakistan, retain the Nikah Nama and the official Marriage Registration Certificate issued through the competent local authority.
In some petitions for a father or stepparent, the marriage record is also part of the evidence establishing the qualifying relationship. Ensure it matches what was submitted to USCIS.

items.title: Prior Marriage Termination Documents
items.sub: Required if the parent beneficiary had a prior marriage that legally ended

sections.c:
• Final divorce decree or divorce registration certificate
  • Annulment order
  • Death certificate of the former spouse
For a Pakistani Muslim divorce, provide the final record issued after completion of the legally required process. A notice of talaq alone may not establish that the divorce became legally effective.
The marital-history dates must match the DS-260 and any records previously submitted to USCIS.

items.title: Death Certificate of Former Spouse
items.sub: Only if the parent's prior marriage ended by death

sections.c: Provide a civil death certificate when the parent beneficiary reports that a prior spouse died.
Include a complete English translation where required by NVC or the interviewing post.

items.title: Father-Child Relationship Evidence
items.sub: Additional proof for certain biological-father cases

sections.c: This may be relevant when the parent beneficiary is the petitioner's biological father and the petitioner's parents were not legally married at the petitioner's birth or the relationship required legitimation or bona fide relationship evidence.

• Parents' marriage or legitimation records
  • Financial-support records
  • School or medical records showing the father's involvement
  • Correspondence, photographs, and co-residence evidence
Even if USCIS approved the I-130, keep the original relationship evidence available for the consular interview.

items.title: Stepparent Relationship Records
items.sub: Marriage and prior-marriage records establishing a qualifying step-relationship

sections.c: For an IR-5 stepparent case, retain the marriage certificate showing that the marriage creating the step-relationship occurred before the petitioner turned 18.
Include proof that any earlier marriages of the biological parent or stepparent legally ended before the qualifying marriage.

items.title: Adoption, Legal Custody, and Joint Residence Records
items.sub: Required in a qualifying adoptive-parent case

sections.c:
• Final adoption decree
  • Legal custody orders
  • Evidence of the required joint residence
  • Any supporting civil records used in the approved I-130 petition
Pakistan generally recognizes guardianship rather than adoption in the same sense used by U.S. immigration law. A guardianship order alone may not establish a qualifying adoptive-parent relationship.

items.title: Name Change or Identity Discrepancy Documents
items.sub: Legal or supporting proof for different names, spellings, dates, or identities

sections.c: Provide documentation if the parent or petitioner's name differs across the passport, birth records, marriage records, I-130 petition, or DS-260.

• Court-issued name-change order
  • Marriage certificate showing a surname change
  • Corrected civil record
  • Old passports, CNIC/NICOP, FRC, or other identity-linking records

items.title: Court and Prison Records
items.sub: Required if the parent was arrested, charged, convicted, or imprisoned

sections.c: Provide certified records for every relevant arrest, charge, conviction, sentence, or court disposition, even where the case was later dismissed or expunged, subject to the applicable instructions.
Follow the Pakistan reciprocity schedule regarding the availability and correct issuing authority for court and prison records.

items.title: Military or Service Records
items.sub: Required if the parent served in the military or armed forces

sections.c: Provide the available military, discharge, retirement, or service-separation record when the parent reports military service.
Use the Pakistan reciprocity schedule to determine which military records are available and acceptable.

items.title: Certified English Translations
items.sub: Required for documents that must be translated under NVC or post instructions

sections.c: Prepare a complete English translation for each document that requires translation under NVC or U.S. Embassy Islamabad instructions.
The translator should certify that the translation is complete and accurate and that the translator is competent to translate from the source language into English.
Keep the original and translation clearly paired. Follow CEAC's current upload instructions for combining or separately uploading the files.
Do not submit a summary or partial translation. Translate all text, stamps, handwritten entries, and annotations that form part of the record.

items.title: Missing Document / Record Unavailability Evidence
items.sub: When a required civil record genuinely cannot be obtained

sections.c:
• Evidence or a statement from the issuing authority regarding unavailability, where obtainable
  • Credible secondary evidence supporting the missing fact
  • A concise explanation identifying the missing record and efforts made to obtain it

Depending on the missing fact and the reciprocity guidance, secondary evidence may include FRC, CRC/B-Form, school records, medical records, vaccination records, older identity documents, or affidavits.
Do not select 'not available' merely because the document is inconvenient to obtain. NVC may reject the submission if the reciprocity schedule shows that the record is available.

items.title: IR-5 Relationship Evidence Backup Set
items.sub: Originals and supporting evidence proving the qualifying parent-child relationship

sections.c: The petitioner's birth certificate is essential, but relationship-specific cases may require additional evidence at interview. Keep the evidence used for the approved I-130 organized and available.

• Petitioner's birth certificate
  • Parents' marriage or legitimation records
  • Father-child relationship evidence, where applicable
  • Stepparent marriage and prior-marriage records
  • Adoption, custody, and joint-residence records
  • Name-discrepancy evidence

items.title: Organized Translation Set
items.sub: Each required translation clearly paired with its source document

sections.c:
• Use clear file names identifying the person and document
  • Keep the source document and translation together or clearly cross-referenced
  • Retain the translator's certification page

items.title: Upload-Ready File Copies
items.sub: Clear, color, properly formatted scans prepared for CEAC

sections.c: Each CEAC file must be no larger than 4 MB. Scan in color, include all pages, and include the reverse side when it contains stamps, seals, handwriting, or other information.
Do not use password-protected, zipped, or editable/modifiable files. PDF is generally preferable for multi-page records, with JPG or JPEG used where appropriate.

• Parent_Passport_Bio.pdf
  • Parent_Birth_Certificate.pdf
  • Petitioner_Birth_Certificate.pdf
  • Pakistan_Police_Certificate.pdf

items.title: Interview Originals and Certified Copies Set
items.sub: Original or certified civil records corresponding to the CEAC uploads

sections.c: The parent beneficiary must bring original or certified copies of the civil documents uploaded to CEAC to the immigrant visa interview.
Keep the interview set separate from the everyday document folder and do not surrender irreplaceable originals except when the consular officer specifically requests them.

guide_card.title: Step-by-Step IR-5 Civil Document Preparation Guide
guide_card.subtitle: Walk through reviewing, scanning, translating, uploading, correcting, and preserving the parent's civil documents for CEAC and interview.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 1 of 13, Sign in to CEAC
tutorial_steps.heading: Sign in to CEAC
tutorial_steps.instruction: Enter CEAC using the NVC Case Number and Invoice ID from the Welcome Letter. Confirm that the required fees show as paid and that the parent beneficiary's DS-260 has been completed before preparing the civil document submission.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Sign in with Case Number and Invoice ID
tutorial_steps.caption: Login credentials are found in your NVC Welcome Letter.
tutorial_steps.note: If both parents are immigrating, use the correct NVC Case Number and Invoice ID for this parent. Each parent has a separate case.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 2 of 13, Confirm IV and AOS fees are paid
tutorial_steps.heading: Confirm all fees are paid
tutorial_steps.instruction: Before document submission begins, verify in CEAC that both the Affidavit of Support fee ($120) and the Immigrant Visa fee ($325) have been successfully processed.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: AOS + IV fees required before document upload
tutorial_steps.caption: If a payment was recently submitted, allow CEAC time to process it. Contact NVC only if the payment remains unresolved or CEAC displays an error.
tutorial_steps.note: The $325 immigrant visa fee is required separately for each parent beneficiary. The AOS fee may cover qualifying related cases processed together, depending on the CEAC case setup.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 3 of 13, Start civil document upload
tutorial_steps.heading: Navigate to the civil documents section
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Navigate to the civil documents section
tutorial_steps.instruction: In CEAC, locate and open the parent beneficiary's civil documents upload area. This is where you will attach the parent's passport biographic page, birth certificate, police certificates, the petitioner's birth certificate, and any case-specific relationship or civil records requested by CEAC.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Begin document submission
tutorial_steps.caption: Review the document list generated for this parent beneficiary before uploading. CEAC creates the list based on the case and DS-260 information.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 4 of 13, Upload documents to CEAC
tutorial_steps.heading: Upload each document individually
tutorial_steps.instruction: Select and upload each civil document under the correct CEAC document category. Each file must be no larger than 4 MB. For a document requiring translation, include the complete source document, complete certified English translation, and translator certification in the file arrangement accepted by the applicable CEAC upload category.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: PDF, JPG, or JPEG files, maximum 4 MB each
tutorial_steps.caption: Upload multi-page records as one complete file in the correct page order whenever possible.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 5 of 13, Upload documents one by one
tutorial_steps.heading: Process each upload sequentially
tutorial_steps.instruction: Continue uploading each remaining document under its matching CEAC category. After each upload, confirm that the correct file name and upload status appear before moving to the next document.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: One document at a time, wait for confirmation
tutorial_steps.caption: Review each category carefully so a document is not uploaded under the wrong heading.
tutorial_steps.note: Do not close or refresh the browser while a file is actively uploading.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 6 of 13, Upload all required documents
tutorial_steps.heading: Complete the full civil document set
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Complete the full civil document set
tutorial_steps.instruction: Upload every document listed as required for the parent beneficiary in CEAC. The core IR-5 set commonly includes the parent's passport biographic page, the parent's birth certificate, required police certificates, and the petitioner's birth certificate establishing the parent-child relationship. Add marriage, divorce, name-change, court, military, father-child, stepparent, adoption, and translation records when applicable.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Required documents checklist completed
tutorial_steps.caption: Use Rahvana's IR-5 civil document checklist together with the case-specific CEAC document list.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 7 of 13, Document unavailable? Use comments
tutorial_steps.heading: Report missing or unavailable documents
tutorial_steps.instruction: If a required record is genuinely unavailable under the issuing country's civil-document rules, use the applicable CEAC unavailable option or comments area. Explain the reason briefly and identify any official unavailability evidence and substitute records submitted.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Use comments to document unavailability
tutorial_steps.caption: Check the Department of State reciprocity schedule before marking a document unavailable.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 8 of 13, Write comments for missing documents
tutorial_steps.heading: Document your explanation in comments
tutorial_steps.instruction: In the comment section, write a clear explanation for any document that is unavailable. Include the document name, reason for unavailability, and any substitute documents submitted. Keep the explanation brief and professional.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Provide context for missing documents
tutorial_steps.caption: Example: 'The issuing authority confirmed that no birth record is available. Uploaded the authority's unavailability statement together with school, vaccination, and family registration records as secondary evidence.'

tutorial_steps.label: Step 9 of 13, Document rejected? Review and correct
tutorial_steps.heading: Review rejection reasons and correct issues
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Review rejection reasons and correct issues
tutorial_steps.instruction: If NVC marks a document as Rejected or Invalid Doc, review the Response Note or document instructions in CEAC. Correct the specific problem, such as the wrong document type, missing pages, poor legibility, an outdated record, an incomplete translation, or an incorrect upload category.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Review rejection reason and resubmit corrected file
tutorial_steps.caption: Follow the specific NVC Response Note rather than assuming the problem is only file size or image quality.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 10 of 13, Re-upload rejected documents
tutorial_steps.heading: Upload the corrected document
tutorial_steps.instruction: After correcting the issue identified by NVC, upload the replacement document under the correct category and submit it again. If the file exceeds 4 MB, compress it without making the text unreadable. If the scan is unclear, rescan it in color at sufficient quality for all text, stamps, seals, and handwriting to remain legible.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Resubmit corrected document
tutorial_steps.caption: Use Rahvana's Document Vault compression tool if file size is the issue.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 11 of 13, Document accepted
tutorial_steps.heading: Confirmation that document was accepted
tutorial_steps.instruction: When NVC accepts a document, CEAC will display the status as 'Accepted.' This means NVC found no correction necessary for that document at the time of review. Continue resolving all remaining document and financial-document requirements.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: File is now in case record
tutorial_steps.caption: An Accepted status applies to that document; documentary completion requires the entire case package to be complete.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 12 of 13, Check submission status
tutorial_steps.heading: Verify your overall submission status
tutorial_steps.instruction: After uploading and submitting the civil documents, verify that each required item shows the appropriate CEAC status. 'Uploaded' means the file has not yet been submitted to NVC; 'Submitted' means it is awaiting NVC review; 'Accepted' means NVC reviewed it and did not request a correction.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Confirm documents are Submitted or Accepted
tutorial_steps.caption: Do not stop at 'Uploaded.' Uploaded files must also be submitted for NVC review.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 13 of 13, Case ready for NVC review
tutorial_steps.heading: Your case is ready for NVC processing
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Your case is ready for NVC processing
tutorial_steps.instruction: Once the required fees, Affidavit of Support package, financial evidence, DS-260, and civil documents have all been submitted, NVC can review the complete case. If all requirements are satisfied, NVC will notify the parties that the case is documentarily complete and will hold it for interview scheduling based on U.S. Embassy or Consulate appointment availability.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Awaiting Documentary Qualification determination
tutorial_steps.caption: Check the official NVC Timeframes page for the current document-review date. Review times change and should not be shown as a fixed 4-8 week estimate.
tutorial_steps.note: Documentary completion does not mean the interview is immediately scheduled. Scheduling depends on post capacity and appointment availability.

financial_requirements.disclaimer: Affidavit of Support thresholds are set by the annual HHS Poverty Guidelines and Form I-864 instructions. Figures below are the rule structure, not a specific year's dollar amounts.
guidance: For an IR-5 parent case, the sponsor generally must demonstrate income at or above 125% of the applicable HHS Poverty Guideline for the sponsor's household size.
The active-duty military 100% exception does not apply when sponsoring a parent.
Household size includes the sponsor, qualifying dependents, the parent beneficiary, certain previously sponsored immigrants, and any other persons required by Form I-864 instructions.
The petitioner must submit Form I-864 even if a joint sponsor is used.
Each additional joint sponsor submits a separate Form I-864.
financial_requirements.source_basis: Form I-864 instructions; HHS Poverty Guidelines; INA 213A, 8 CFR 213a.

guide_card.title: Step-by-Step Affidavit of Support Guide
guide_card.subtitle: Walk through paying sponsorship fees, submitting financial documents, and uploading supporting evidence to CEAC.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 1 of 8, Pay Affidavit of Support fee
tutorial_steps.heading: Pay the AOS sponsorship fee
tutorial_steps.instruction: In CEAC, navigate to the fee section and pay the Affidavit of Support fee ($120 as of 2026). This fee is required before financial documentation can be submitted. Use your CEAC account to complete the payment.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: $120 required payment
tutorial_steps.caption: AOS fee is separate from the Immigrant Visa fee, both must be paid before document submission.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 2 of 8, Receive AOS payment receipt
tutorial_steps.heading: Confirm payment and save receipt
tutorial_steps.instruction: After successfully paying the AOS fee, CEAC will display a payment receipt or confirmation. Save or print this confirmation for your records as proof that the fee has been paid.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Save receipt for your records
tutorial_steps.caption: The receipt confirms the fee payment and allows you to proceed with submitting sponsorship documents.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 3 of 8, Start AOS and financial document submission
tutorial_steps.heading: Begin the Affidavit of Support document submission
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Begin the Affidavit of Support document submission
tutorial_steps.instruction: Once the AOS fee is paid, navigate to the Affidavit of Support section in CEAC. This is where you will upload the completed I-864 or I-864EZ form and all supporting financial documents for the petitioner and any joint sponsors or household members.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Prepare to upload AOS forms and financial evidence
tutorial_steps.caption: Have the signed Form I-864, most recent required tax evidence, proof of sponsor status and domicile, and any current-income, asset, household-member, or joint-sponsor evidence applicable to the case.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 4 of 8, Select and verify document type
tutorial_steps.heading: Check the document type before uploading
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Check the document type before uploading
tutorial_steps.instruction: CEAC requires you to specify the document type for each file (e.g., Tax Return, W-2, Affidavit of Support form, etc.). Verify that you are selecting the correct document type from CEAC's dropdown menu before uploading each file.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Verify correct type before upload
tutorial_steps.caption: Incorrectly classified documents may be rejected or cause confusion during NVC review, always verify the type first.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 5 of 8, Upload financial documents
tutorial_steps.heading: Upload each financial document
tutorial_steps.instruction: Upload the signed Form I-864 and the financial evidence required for each sponsor. This commonly includes the most recent IRS tax transcript or qualifying federal tax return and any W-2s or schedules needed to establish individual income. Add current pay evidence, employment verification, asset records, non-filing evidence, domicile evidence, household-member documents, or joint-sponsor evidence where applicable.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Tax returns, W-2s, pay stubs, bank statements
tutorial_steps.caption: Upload files in the order they are requested by CEAC to keep the submission organized.
tutorial_steps.note: Do not close the browser tab during the upload process.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 6 of 8, Verify submission completeness
tutorial_steps.heading: Check that all documents are submitted
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Check that all documents are submitted
tutorial_steps.instruction: After uploading all financial documents, review the submission checklist in CEAC to confirm that all required documents have been received and are marked as 'Submitted' or 'Accepted.' This ensures your AOS package is complete.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: All required AOS documents submitted
tutorial_steps.caption: A complete AOS submission is necessary for NVC to determine documentary qualification.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 7 of 8, Document rejected? Review reason
tutorial_steps.heading: Understand why a document was rejected
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Understand why a document was rejected
tutorial_steps.instruction: If a financial document is rejected by CEAC, you will see a rejection reason. Common reasons include: file too large (over 4 MB), image too blurry, missing pages, or incorrect document type. Review the reason carefully and prepare a corrected version.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Review reason and prepare corrected file
tutorial_steps.caption: Follow the NVC response note. Rescan unclear documents in color at sufficient quality for all text and signatures to remain readable, and keep each file within CEAC's current size limit.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 8 of 8, Replace rejected document
tutorial_steps.heading: Re-upload the corrected document
tutorial_steps.instruction: After correcting the issue, re-upload the document using CEAC's resubmission process. Ensure the new file meets all requirements: under 4 MB, clear and legible, correct document type selected. Upload and wait for confirmation that the document is now accepted.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Resubmit corrected financial document
tutorial_steps.caption: After the corrected document is submitted, monitor CEAC for NVC review. The AOS portion is complete only when all required sponsor forms and financial evidence have been accepted.

sponsor_required.title: Form I-864, ${sp}
sponsor_required.sub: Completed Affidavit of Support for the IR-5 parent beneficiary

guide.intro: Each sponsor must submit a separate, properly completed Form I-864. The petitioner must submit Form I-864 even when a joint sponsor is used.

sections.title: USCIS Form Integrity
sections.body: Download the latest version of Form I-864 directly from the USCIS website. Fill out all pages, leave no blank fields (use 'N/A' or 'None' where appropriate), and ensure it is signed. NVC will reject the form if pages are missing, the signature is photocopied/digital instead of wet-ink/original (if required by current post rules), or if the form edition is outdated.

sections.title: Household size and Income
sections.body: Ensure the household size on Part 5 matches the tax return information or is correctly adjusted. The sponsor's current individual annual income (Part 6) must align with the supporting employment letters, W-2s, and pay stubs. If the petitioner's income is $0, they must still file Form I-864 showing $0 income, and a joint sponsor will file a separate I-864.

sections.title: IR-5 specific rules
sections.body: Form I-864EZ should NOT be used for an IR-5 parent visa case if there are multiple sponsors, joint sponsors, or if the petitioner is combining income. Stick to the standard Form I-864 to avoid administrative processing delays.

sponsor_required.title: Most Recent IRS Tax Transcript, ${sp}
sponsor_required.sub: Preferred official tax evidence for the most recent tax year

guide.intro: An IRS tax transcript from the most recent tax year is the preferred tax evidence because it can be reviewed more efficiently than a copy of a tax return.

sections.title: Why IRS Transcripts are Preferred
sections.body: The NVC strongly prefers IRS Tax Transcripts over paper-filed Form 1040 returns because transcripts are verified directly by the IRS, reducing verification delays. It shows the Adjusted Gross Income (AGI), tax liability, and filing status clearly.

sections.title: How to Obtain
sections.body: The sponsor can obtain the transcript instantly by logging into their online IRS account via the 'Get Transcript Online' tool. If they cannot access the online tool, they must request it by mail using IRS Form 4506-T. Ensure you download the 'Tax Return Transcript' (not the Account Transcript).

sections.title: Alternative
sections.body: If an IRS transcript is genuinely unavailable, you must submit a complete, signed copy of the federal income tax return (Form 1040) along with all W-2s, 1099s, and supporting schedules.

sponsor_required.title: Proof of U.S. Status, ${sp}
sponsor_required.sub: Evidence that the sponsor has qualifying U.S. immigration status

guide.intro: The IR-5 petitioner must be a U.S. citizen. A joint sponsor may be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or lawful permanent resident, as permitted by the current Form I-864 rules.

sections.title: Accepted Citizenship Evidence
sections.body:
Provide a clear color scan of one of the following:
  • A current, unexpired U.S. passport biographic page.
  • U.S. birth certificate showing birth in the United States.
  • Certificate of Naturalization (Form N-550 or N-570).
  • Certificate of Citizenship (Form N-560 or N-561).

sections.title: Joint Sponsor (LPR Status)
sections.body: If the joint sponsor is a Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR), they must provide a clear color scan of both sides of their Permanent Resident Card (Green Card, Form I-551). The card must be unexpired.

sponsor_required.title: Proof of U.S. Domicile, ${sp}
sponsor_required.sub: Evidence of domicile in the United States or qualifying steps to re-establish it

guide.intro: Every Form I-864 sponsor must be domiciled in the United States or demonstrate qualifying steps to re-establish U.S. domicile no later than the intending immigrant's admission.

sections.title: What is Domicile?
sections.body: Domicile is the place where a sponsor has their principal, permanent home and intends to maintain it. For petitioners living in the U.S., a driver's license, utility bills, tax history, and employment records are sufficient.

sections.title: Petitioners Residing in Pakistan
sections.body:
If the U.S. citizen petitioner is currently living in Pakistan, they must provide strong documentary evidence that they have taken concrete steps to re-establish U.S. domicile before or at the same time the parent enters the U.S. Acceptable evidence includes:
  • A U.S. residential lease agreement or proof of U.S. home ownership.
  • A signed employment contract or job offer in the U.S.
  • Documentation showing U.S. bank accounts, voter registration, and active driver's license.
  • Proof of enrolling children in U.S. schools.

sponsor_conditional.title: Complete Federal Tax Return, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Alternative when the most recent IRS tax transcript is unavailable or specifically requested

guide.intro: A complete copy of the most recent filed federal income tax return may be used instead of an IRS transcript or when NVC specifically requests the complete return.

sections.title: Complete Return Assembly
sections.body:
A complete return means you must include:
  • Form 1040 (all pages, signed and dated by the sponsor).
  • All W-2 and 1099 statements showing wages and earnings.
  • All schedules filed with the IRS (Schedule A, B, C, D, E, etc.).
If any schedule is missing, NVC will issue a rejection notice.

sponsor_conditional.title: W-2, 1099, and Relevant Tax Schedules, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Supporting records when needed to establish the sponsor's individual income

guide.intro: These records may be needed when a complete tax return is submitted, the sponsor filed jointly, or the transcript does not clearly establish the sponsor's individual qualifying income.

sections.title: Isolating Joint Filing Income
sections.body: If the sponsor filed a joint tax return with their spouse, their individual income must be verified separately. Uploading all individual W-2 and 1099 forms isolates the sponsor's own earnings from their spouse's earnings, ensuring they meet the 125% Federal Poverty Guidelines on their own.

sponsor_conditional.title: Current Pay Records, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Current income evidence when ongoing earnings must be established

guide.intro: Recent pay records can establish that the sponsor's qualifying income is current and continuing, especially when income changed after the most recent tax filing.

sections.title: Current Income Proof
sections.body: Provide consecutive pay stubs covering the last 6 months. Pay stubs must show the employer's name, employee name, gross wages, pay period, and year-to-date earnings. This is crucial if the sponsor's income has increased since their last tax filing or if they recently started a new job.

sponsor_conditional.title: Employment Verification Letter, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Supporting proof of current employment and compensation

guide.intro: An employment verification letter may support current qualifying income where employment evidence is needed.

sections.title: Letter Specifications
sections.body:
The letter must be printed on official company letterhead, dated within the last 60 days, and signed by an authorized supervisor or HR manager. It must state:
  • Dates of employment and job title.
  • Employment status (full-time, part-time, permanent).
  • Annual salary or hourly wage rate and average weekly hours.

sponsor_conditional.title: Asset Evidence, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Required only when qualifying assets are used to cover an income shortfall

guide.intro: Qualifying assets may be used when income alone is insufficient. For an IR-5 parent case, the net value of qualifying assets generally must equal at least five times the income shortfall.

sections.title: Asset Valuation Requirements
sections.body: Provide proof of ownership, current valuation, and evidence that the asset can be converted to cash within 12 months. For real estate, submit the deed, a professional appraisal, and a mortgage statement showing current equity. For bank accounts, submit 12 months of consecutive monthly statements.

sections.title: Five-Times Rule for Parents
sections.body: For immediate relative categories (which includes the parent of a U.S. citizen), the total net value of assets must equal at least 5 times the difference between the sponsor's income and the 125% poverty guideline line.

sponsor_conditional.title: Tax Non-Filing Explanation, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Required if the sponsor was not legally required to file the most recent federal tax return

guide.intro: A sponsor who did not file a federal tax return must explain why filing was not legally required.

sections.title: Filing Thresholds and Exemptions
sections.body: Sponsors who had no U.S. income or whose income fell below the IRS filing threshold must provide a written, signed statement citing the specific IRS code or threshold limits. If they were living abroad and did not file, they must explain this, keeping in mind that U.S. citizens are required to file taxes on worldwide income.

sponsor_recommended.title: Organized Sponsorship Packet, ${sp}
sponsor_recommended.sub: Affidavit form and supporting evidence grouped clearly by sponsor

guide.intro: Each sponsor's records should be kept separate and clearly labeled so the correct form and evidence are uploaded under the correct sponsor in CEAC.

sections.title: How to organize
sections.body: Group Form I-864, tax evidence, status evidence, domicile evidence, current-income evidence, and asset evidence for ${sp} into one clearly labeled folder structure.

household_conditional.title: Form I-864A, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: Contract for a qualifying household member contributing income or assets

guide.intro: A qualifying household member whose income or assets are used generally completes and signs Form I-864A with the petitioning sponsor.

sections.title: Form I-864A Contract
sections.body: Form I-864A is a legally binding contract between the sponsor and the household member. The household member agrees to be jointly and severally liable for the financial support of the parent beneficiary. Ensure all pages are submitted and signed in ink.

household_conditional.title: Most Recent Tax Evidence, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: IRS transcript or applicable federal return evidence for the household member

guide.intro: The household member must document the income or assets contributed through Form I-864A.

sections.title: Tax Records for Household Members
sections.body: Provide the IRS Tax Transcript for the household member's most recent tax year. If transcripts are not available, submit Form 1040 accompanied by W-2s and schedules.

household_conditional.title: Current Income Evidence, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: Proof that the household member's contributed income is current and continuing

guide.intro: Current income evidence should support the amount contributed by the household member on Form I-864A.

sections.title: Verifying Continuing Income
sections.body: Provide current pay stubs and employment letters for the household member. The income must be from a lawful source and expected to continue after the parent immigrates.

household_conditional.title: Proof of Household Relationship or Shared Residence, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: Evidence establishing eligibility to contribute through Form I-864A

guide.intro: Depending on the household member category, evidence of a qualifying family relationship, shared residence, or both may be required.

sections.title: Establishing Household Linkage
sections.body: If the household member is the sponsor's spouse, sibling, child, or parent, submit birth certificates, marriage certificates, or adoption decrees. Also submit lease agreements, tax filings, or utility bills showing they share the same physical residence.

household_conditional.title: Household Member Asset Evidence, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: Required only when the household member's assets are included

guide.intro: Include asset evidence only when the household member's qualifying assets are being used in the sponsorship calculation.

sections.title: What to establish
sections.body: Show ownership, net value after liabilities, and convertibility to cash within one year without undue hardship.

general_recommended.title: Prior-Year Tax Evidence Backup
general_recommended.sub: Additional prior-year records available if NVC requests them

guide.intro: The most recent tax year is the normal core evidence, but earlier records may be useful when income history is irregular or NVC requests additional documentation.

sections.title: When it may help
sections.body: Keep prior-year transcripts or returns available when recent income changed substantially, a filing extension or non-filing issue exists, or additional income history is requested.

general_recommended.title: Upload-Ready Financial Packet
general_recommended.sub: Clear, properly named files organized for CEAC upload

guide.intro: Preparing an upload-ready packet reduces classification, readability, and submission errors.

sections.title: File preparation
sections.body: Keep each file within CEAC's current size limit, use an accepted file type, make every page legible, and organize files separately for the petitioner, each joint sponsor, and each household member.

joint_sponsor_requirements.disclaimer: A joint sponsor is only needed when the petitioner cannot meet the income requirement alone. Advisory guidance, confirm against the current Form I-864/I-864A instructions.
guidance: A joint sponsor must be a U.S. citizen or LPR, at least 18, and domiciled in the United States.

The joint sponsor must independently satisfy the applicable 125% requirement for the joint sponsor's household size, including the IR-5 parent beneficiary and all other persons required by Form I-864 instructions. The petitioner's income is not combined with the joint sponsor's income.
A household member who is not the sponsor uses Form I-864A to contribute their income.
The joint sponsor submits their own federal tax returns and proof of status.
joint_sponsor_requirements.source_basis: Form I-864 / I-864A instructions; INA 213A, 8 CFR 213a.2.

guideSteps.label: Step 1 of 5
guideSteps.heading: What is the polio vaccination requirement?
guideSteps.instruction: Typical cases from Pakistan will require a polio certificate for the medical examination. Therefore, it is highly recommended and advisable to obtain it beforehand to avoid any delays in your medical process.

visual.title: Why this is required
visual.sub: The U.S. requires polio vaccination documentation from applicants from polio-endemic countries. This is administered at an approved vaccination site, not a general clinic.

guideSteps.label: Step 2 of 5
guideSteps.heading: Where to get vaccinated
guideSteps.instruction: Polio vaccinations for visa purposes must be obtained from an approved government vaccination post or official WHO-designated site. Do not use a private clinic unless it is specifically on the approved list.
guideSteps.note: Do not go to a general doctor or hospital for this, you must use a government-approved site for the certificate to be accepted.

visual.title: Approved Vaccination Sites
visual.sub: Government immunization centres in major cities typically administer this vaccine and issue the official certificate. Contact your local district health office or check with your panel physician for the nearest site.

guideSteps.label: Step 3 of 5
guideSteps.heading: What the certificate looks like
guideSteps.instruction: The official polio vaccination certificate is typically a printed card or letter issued at the vaccination site. It should include your name, vaccination date, and the type of vaccine received.

visual.title: Certificate Details to Verify
items: Your full legal name (matching passport)
Date of vaccination
Vaccine type, oral polio vaccine (OPV)
Official stamp or signature

guideSteps.label: Step 4 of 5
guideSteps.heading: Timing, when to get vaccinated
guideSteps.instruction: Get your polio vaccination at least a few days before your medical exam appointment so you can bring the original certificate to the exam. The panel physician will record it as part of your medical packet.
guideSteps.note: Do not get vaccinated the same day as the medical exam unless your physician specifically confirms this is acceptable.

visual.title: Recommended Timing
visual.sub: Vaccinate → Receive certificate → Bring original to medical exam. Budget at least 1-3 days between vaccination and your scheduled medical exam date.

guideSteps.label: Step 5 of 5
guideSteps.heading: Bring the original certificate to your medical exam
guideSteps.instruction: Bring the original polio vaccination certificate to your medical exam appointment. Your panel physician will review it and include documentation in the sealed medical packet sent to the embassy.

visual.sub: Return to this step and mark the polio certificate as obtained once you have it in hand.

steps.step_description: Assemble the original or certified hard-copy documents needed for the parent beneficiary's IR-5 consular interview. Review each item and organize the packet carefully before interview day.
actions: Collect all original or certified documents

items.title: Current Passport and Relevant Prior Passports
items.sub: Current unexpired passport plus prior passports containing relevant U.S. visa or travel history

sections.c: Bring the parent beneficiary's current original passport, which must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the intended date of entry into the United States. Also bring all prior passports, especially those containing previous U.S. visas, travel stamps, visa refusals, or immigration history from any country. Do not leave older passports at home, the consular officer will review them to assess full travel history.
Bring one clear photocopy of the current passport biographic page (the page with the photo, name, DOB, and expiry date). Keep the photocopy in a separate section from the original passport.
The passport must be signed by the parent in the designated signature field. An unsigned passport may be flagged at the interview window.

items.title: Parent Beneficiary's Original Birth Certificate
items.sub: Original or certified civil birth record, translation, and photocopy

sections.c:
Bring the original Birth Registration Certificate issued by the authority responsible for registering the beneficiary's birth:

  • Union Council
  • Municipal Corporation
  • Capital Development Authority (CDA) — Islamabad
  • Cantonment Board

Select the issuing authority that applies to your birth record and bring the original document.

If the birth certificate is in Urdu only, bring the original certified English translation alongside it. Also bring one clear photocopy of the full birth certificate (both sides, if stamped on the reverse).

If the birth was never registered and you submitted a Non-Availability Certificate (NAC) to NVC, bring the original signed and stamped NAC from the Union Council, along with all original secondary records (school certificate, B-Form, family affidavits) that were uploaded to CEAC.
Confirm that the parent's name, date of birth, place of birth, and parents' names match the passport, DS-260, and CEAC records exactly. Any discrepancies must be explained with supporting documents.

items.title: Petitioner's Original or Certified Birth Certificate
items.sub: Core IR-5 record showing the parent-child relationship

sections.c: Bring the U.S. citizen petitioner's original birth certificate or a certified copy issued directly by the state/county registrar showing the parent beneficiary named as the petitioner's mother or father. This is the core document establishing the qualifying IR-5 parent-child relationship. A personal printout or photocopy of the document previously uploaded to CEAC is NOT sufficient.
If the petitioner's birth certificate is not in English, bring a complete certified English translation. Also bring one clear photocopy for the embassy's records.

The parent beneficiary must be clearly listed by name on the petitioner's birth certificate. If the name is abbreviated, differs in spelling, or is missing, bring supporting identity-linking documents (One-and-the-Same Affidavit or corrected NADRA records).

items.title: Birth Certificates for All of the Parent Beneficiary's Children
items.sub: Original or certified copies for every child, including children not immigrating

sections.c: Bring the original birth certificates for all children of the parent beneficiary, including the petitioner and all siblings, regardless of their age, marital status, or immigration status. In Pakistan, each must be an original NADRA Computerized Birth Registration Certificate (CBRC). Do not substitute photocopies.

The consular officer reviews these records to verify the parent's complete family structure, confirm sibling relationships, and cross-reference dates of birth with the parent's marital and civil history. Missing children's birth certificates can cause delays at the interview window.
Bring certified English translations for any Urdu-only certificates, and one photocopy of each record. Keep each original paired with its translation.

items.title: Original Police Clearance Certificate
items.sub: The PCC obtained for this interview cycle

sections.c: Bring the original PCC obtained for your interview. Do not bring the older PCC submitted during NVC processing; bring the PCC intended for your current interview.

Confirm the issue date on the PCC. If the PCC was obtained more than 12 months before the interview date, a fresh one must be obtained from the District Police Officer (DPO) office or Khidmat Markaz before attending the interview.

If the parent resided in other countries for more than 12 months after age 16, bring the original police certificates from those countries as well. If a foreign PCC was uploaded to CEAC, the embassy may ask to see the original physical document at the interview window.

items.title: NVC Interview Appointment Letter
items.sub: Printed copy of the interview appointment notice

sections.c: Print and bring a copy of the NVC interview appointment letter for the parent beneficiary.

items.title: Form I-864, Petitioner
items.sub: The petitioner's completed Affidavit of Support package

sections.c: Bring the original signed Affidavit of Support. This must be the wet-ink signed original, not a photocopy.
The petitioner must provide Form I-864 even when a joint sponsor is used. Both the petitioner's I-864 and the joint sponsor's separate I-864 should be in the packet.
Ensure the copy you bring is the same completed version submitted to NVC, not a blank or revised edition. The form must be signed in ink by the petitioner.

items.title: Most Recent Tax Evidence, Petitioner
items.sub: IRS transcript or most recent federal return with related income records

sections.c: Bring a printed copy of the petitioner's IRS Tax Return Transcript for the most recent tax year. If an IRS transcript was not used, bring the complete signed Form 1040 with all W-2s, 1099s, and applicable schedules. Keep these matched and organized as a single packet.

If the NVC submission was in a prior tax year and a new tax year has since ended, bring the tax documents for the more recent year as well. The consular officer will review the most current evidence of income.

If the petitioner's income or employment changed significantly after NVC submission, bring supporting current-income evidence: recent pay stubs covering the past 3-6 months and an employer verification letter on official letterhead.

items.title: Petitioner's U.S. Citizenship and Domicile Evidence
items.sub: Proof of U.S. citizenship and U.S. domicile or re-establishment of domicile

sections.c:
Bring a clear photocopy of the petitioner's proof of U.S. citizenship:

  • U.S. passport biographic page (current and valid)
  • U.S. birth certificate showing birth in the United States
  • Certificate of Naturalization (Form N-550 or N-570)
  • Certificate of Citizenship (Form N-560 or N-561)

Bring copies of documents proving that the petitioner maintains a permanent home in the United States: utility bills, lease agreement or mortgage statement, pay stubs, U.S. driver's license, bank account statements, voter registration, or property tax records.

If the petitioner is currently residing in Pakistan or another country, bring strong documentary evidence of concrete steps taken to re-establish U.S. domicile, such as a signed U.S. job offer letter, a signed U.S. residential lease, or enrollment of children in U.S. schools.

items.title: Joint Sponsor or Household Member Package
items.sub: Required only if a joint sponsor or household member is used

sections.c:
If a joint sponsor was used, bring a complete photocopy packet for the joint sponsor:

  • Signed Form I-864 (all pages)
  • IRS Tax Transcript or complete tax return for the most recent year (with W-2s and schedules)
  • Proof of U.S. citizenship (passport biographic page, Certificate of Naturalization) or LPR status (both sides of the Permanent Resident Card)
  • Proof of U.S. domicile (utility bills, lease, driver's license, pay stubs)

If a household member's income or assets were included via Form I-864A, bring the signed Form I-864A together with the household member's tax transcript or return, pay stubs, and employment letter as applicable.

groups.label: Bring, Interview Day and Conditional Documents

items.title: DS-260 Confirmation Page
items.sub: Printed Immigrant Visa Application confirmation page

items.title: DS-260 Confirmation Page
items.sub: Online Immigrant Visa Application Confirmation

sections.c: Bring the printed DS-260 confirmation page with barcode. This confirms you have successfully submitted your online immigrant visa application.
Make sure all information in your DS-260 form is accurate and matches your supporting documents such as passport and civil records.
You can download and print the confirmation page after submitting your DS-260 form from the Consular Electronic Application Center (CEAC) website.

items.title: Two Recent Visa Photographs
items.sub: Two identical 5 cm × 5 cm color photographs

sections.c:
Bring exactly two recent, identical color photographs of the parent beneficiary taken within the last 6 months. The photos must meet U.S. visa specifications:

  • Size: 2 inches × 2 inches (51 mm × 51 mm)
  • Background: plain white or off-white
  • Head must be centered, facing the camera, with a neutral expression
  • Eyes fully open
  • No eyeglasses
  • Head coverings permitted only for religious reasons, and must not cast shadows on the face
Obtain photos at a professional photo studio familiar with U.S. visa standards. Photos taken at local shops may use incorrect dimensions or background colors, confirm specifications before printing.

items.title: Medical Examination Results
items.sub: Sealed medical results provided by the physician or sent directly to the embassy

sections.c: The U.S. Embassy-approved panel physician in Pakistan will either transmit the medical examination results directly and electronically to U.S. Embassy Islamabad, or give the parent beneficiary a sealed envelope containing the results. Both are accepted, check with the clinic about which method they use.

sections.t: If a sealed envelope is provided
sections.c: Do not open the envelope under any circumstances. An opened medical envelope will be rejected at the consular window and the medical examination may need to be repeated. Bring the sealed envelope directly to the interview and hand it to the consular officer.

Panel physicians approved by U.S. Embassy Islamabad operate in Islamabad, Lahore, and Karachi. Only results from an approved panel physician are accepted for the immigrant visa interview. Do not use a general clinic or hospital not on the embassy's approved list.

items.title: Parent Beneficiary's Marriage Certificate
items.sub: Required if the parent is married or the marriage is relevant to the relationship history

sections.c: Bring the original marriage certificate or a certified copy, together with any required certified English translation and one photocopy. Both the original and the translation should be clearly paired in the same section of the folder.
For a Pakistani Muslim marriage, bring both the original Urdu Nikah Nama (with a full certified English translation) and the bilingual NADRA Marriage Registration Certificate (MRC).
Verify that the names of both spouses and the date of marriage on the Nikah Nama and MRC match all other civil records and the DS-260 exactly.

items.title: Prior Marriage Termination Records
items.sub: Required if the parent beneficiary was previously married

sections.c: Bring the original or certified final divorce record, annulment order, or former spouse's death certificate for every prior marriage of the parent beneficiary. All prior marriages must be accounted for, do not leave out any prior marriage even if it ended many years ago.

For a Pakistani Muslim divorce, the required document is the final computerized Union Council Divorce Certificate issued after the 90-day Talaq notification period. A private Talaqnama or notice of Talaq alone is not accepted. If the divorce was court-ordered (Khula), bring the certified court decree and the Union Council registration certificate.
Include a certified English translation for any Urdu or other non-English records, and bring one photocopy of each document paired with its original.

items.title: Additional Father-Child Relationship Evidence
items.sub: Required in certain biological-father cases

sections.c: Bring the original evidence used in the approved I-130 if the case required legitimation or proof of a bona fide father-child relationship.

• Parents' marriage or legitimation records
  • Financial support and co-residence evidence
  • School, medical, religious, or government records
  • Correspondence and photographs

items.title: Stepparent Relationship Records
items.sub: Required for an IR-5 stepparent case

sections.c: Bring the original marriage certificate showing that the marriage creating the step-relationship occurred before the petitioner turned 18.
Also bring records proving that all prior marriages of the biological parent and stepparent legally ended.

items.title: Adoption, Custody, and Joint Residence Records
items.sub: Required for a qualifying adoptive-parent case

sections.c: Bring the original or certified adoption decree, legal custody records, and evidence of the required joint residence used to establish the approved relationship.
Pakistani guardianship documentation does not automatically establish an adoption qualifying under U.S. immigration law.

items.title: Name Change or Identity-Linking Records
items.sub: Required when names or identity details differ across records

sections.c: Bring original or certified records linking different names, spellings, dates, or identities appearing across the case documents.

items.title: Court and Criminal Records
items.sub: Required if the parent was arrested, charged, convicted, or imprisoned

sections.c: Bring original or certified court and criminal records for each applicable incident, with certified English translations and photocopies.

items.title: Military Records
items.sub: Required if the parent served in any country's military

sections.c: Bring the available original or certified military service, discharge, or retirement records, together with required English translations and photocopies.

items.title: Passport Delivery Registration Confirmation
items.sub: Printed proof of online passport return or pickup registration

sections.c: Bring a printed copy of the registration confirmation showing the parent beneficiary's selected passport return or pickup location.
Verify that the parent's passport number and contact information are correct.
Use the current registration portal linked from the official U.S. Embassy Islamabad immigrant visa instructions.

items.title: Labeled Folder System
items.sub: Simple sections separating originals, translations, and photocopies

sections.c: A clearly organized packet helps the parent beneficiary produce each requested document quickly.

• Use lightweight labeled folders
  • Separate Passport and Appointment / Civil Records / IR-5 Relationship / Financial Sponsor / Conditional Records
  • Keep each original together with its translation and photocopy

items.title: Complete Photocopy Set
items.sub: One clear copy of each civil and relationship document

sections.c: The embassy may retain photocopies while returning original civil documents after the interview.

items.title: CEAC-to-Original Match Check
items.sub: Verify that interview originals match the documents uploaded to CEAC

sections.c: Compare each original or certified document against the file uploaded to CEAC. Upload any required updated document before the interview when instructed.
Confirm names, dates, issuing authorities, translations, page completeness, and police-certificate validity.

tutorial.label: Step 1 of 8
tutorial.heading: Prepare the night before
tutorial.instruction: The night before your interview, lay out your complete document packet, confirm your appointment letter is printed, and ensure your transport to the embassy is planned. Do not leave anything to the morning.

tutorial.label: Step 2 of 8
tutorial.heading: Arrive early, embassy entry is strict
tutorial.instruction: Arrive at the embassy at least 20–30 minutes before your scheduled appointment time. Embassy security queues can be slow. Latecomers may not be admitted for their scheduled slot.
tutorial.note: Do not carry electronics beyond what is permitted by the embassy. Check the specific embassy's guidelines on phones and devices before arrival.
tutorial.visual:
Arrival guidance
Plan for 20-30 minutes of buffer time. Factor in travel to the Diplomatic Enclave, transport arrangements, and security screening at U.S. Embassy Islamabad.
Earlier is always safer than exactly on time

tutorial.label: Step 3 of 8
tutorial.heading: Security screening and document intake
tutorial.instruction: At entry, your appointment letter and passport will be checked. You will pass through security screening. Some items, including certain electronics, may need to be left outside or checked in.
tutorial.visual:
Entry sequence
Appointment letter check at gate
Security screening (bag + personal)
Document receipt / number assignment
Wait in designated area

tutorial.label: Step 4 of 8
tutorial.heading: Biometrics, fingerprints and photo
tutorial.instruction: Before your consular interview, you will be called to provide biometrics, fingerprints and a digital photograph. This is routine and applies to almost all immigrant visa applicants.
tutorial.visual:
Biometric collection
Fingerprints are scanned digitally. You will also be photographed. This takes only a few minutes. Follow the staff instructions exactly.

tutorial.label: Step 5 of 8
tutorial.heading: The consular interview window
tutorial.instruction: You will be called to a consular window. The officer may ask about the parent-child relationship, family history, civil records, financial sponsorship, intended U.S. residence, medical admissibility, and prior immigration or travel history. Answer each question truthfully and directly.
tutorial.note: Consistency is critical. Your answers must align with your DS-260 responses and the documents you submitted during NVC processing.
tutorial.visual:
Common IR-5 interview topics
What is your relationship to the petitioner?
When and where was the petitioner born?
Where does the petitioner live and what do they do?
Where will you live in the United States?
Do you have any other children?
Have you visited or applied for a visa to the United States before?

tutorial.label: Step 6 of 8
tutorial.heading: Document review at the window
tutorial.instruction: The officer may ask you to produce specific original documents. Present them calmly and in the order requested. Having a well-organized packet makes this faster and smoother.
tutorial.visual:
Be ready to produce
Current passport and relevant prior passports
Parent beneficiary's birth certificate
Petitioner's original or certified birth certificate
Birth certificates for the parent's children
Original valid police certificate
Form I-864 and financial evidence
Relationship-specific records if applicable
Two visa photographs

tutorial.label: Step 7 of 8
tutorial.heading: Stay calm, the officer is doing their job
tutorial.instruction: Consular officers ask direct questions. Their tone is professional, not personal. Nervousness is expected and normal. Answer clearly and calmly. If you do not understand a question, politely ask for clarification.
tutorial.visual: Answer only what is asked. Be honest. Be calm. Be concise. You have prepared for this, trust your preparation.

tutorial.label: Step 8 of 8
tutorial.heading: Possible outcomes after the interview
tutorial.instruction: The officer will indicate the outcome at the window or shortly after. After the interview, your application may be approved, refused under applicable law (including 221(g) where applicable), or require further administrative processing before a final determination is completed. If you were given a 221(g) refusal letter, continue to Step 9 for Rahvana’s AP guidance.
tutorial.visual:

Approved, visa issuance processing begins Approved
221(g) refusal, documents or administrative processing required Further action
Refused under another legal ground, review the written notice Legal ground

items: Arriving without the printed appointment letter
Bringing electronic devices that are prohibited beyond security

info_sections.title: What to do while waiting
items: Check your CEAC status approximately once a week and record any changes.
Monitor the email address registered with the embassy for additional requests or updates.
Respond promptly if the embassy requests further documents or information.
Ensure your passport remains valid throughout the review process.

For Administrative Processing inquiries, follow the Embassy’s current instructions for your case. The Department of State generally recommends allowing up to 180 days from the interview or submission of supplemental documents, whichever is later, for Administrative Processing. This is a general guideline, not a requirement to wait 180 days before making an inquiry. If you have concerns about your case or believe an inquiry is appropriate, check the Embassy’s latest guidance and contact them through the appropriate channel.

uscis_tutorial_steps.note: Use a personal email address the petitioner actively monitors. All USCIS notices, including Requests for Evidence, will be sent here. Do not use a shared or work email.

uscis_tutorial_steps.label: Step 3, Create a strong password
uscis_tutorial_steps.heading: Set up a secure password
uscis_tutorial_steps.instruction: Create a password between 8 and 64 characters. You may use letters, numbers, and special characters. Enter it twice to confirm.

uscis_tutorial_steps.label: Step 4, Set up two-step verification
uscis_tutorial_steps.heading: Choose a verification method
uscis_tutorial_steps.instruction: USCIS requires two-step verification on every login. Choose one method: authentication app (most secure), SMS text message, or email. You'll also receive a one-time backup code, save it somewhere safe.
uscis_tutorial_steps.note: Save the backup code that appears after setup. If you lose access to your verification method (e.g. a new phone), this code is the only way to recover account access.

uscis_tutorial_steps.heading: Set up your 5 security questions
uscis_tutorial_steps.instruction: USCIS requires you to select and answer five security questions. These are used to verify your identity if you need to reset your password. Choose questions with answers only you would know.
uscis_tutorial_steps.note: Write down your questions and answers somewhere safe, ideally in a secure password manager. You will also be asked to enter these in Rahvana's Portal Wallet for safekeeping.

uscis_tutorial_steps.label: Step 6, Select account type and finish

uscis_tutorial_steps.instruction: After verification, you'll see a "Welcome to your USCIS Account" screen. Select myUSCIS, then choose "I am an applicant, petitioner, or requestor" and click Submit. A confirmation email will arrive from myaccount@uscis.dhs.gov.
